title: Chapter 3 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Pre‑rendering & Data Fetching!

questions.question: Which rendering mode sends an almost empty HTML page and relies on JavaScript to build the UI?
questions.explanation: CSR sends a bare HTML shell and all rendering happens in the browser.

questions.question: What must `getStaticProps` return at minimum?
questions.explanation: The `props` object is mandatory; everything else is optional.

questions.question: `getStaticProps` runs on the client side.
questions.explanation: It runs only at build time on the server, never in the browser.

questions.question: What does `getStaticPaths` do?
options: Defines all available dynamic routes for static generation
questions.explanation: It tells Next.js which paths to pre‑render for a dynamic page.

questions.question: Which `fallback` option shows a loading state while the page is being generated?
questions.explanation: `fallback: true` allows the page to show a loading state using `router.isFallback` before the content arrives.

questions.question: When does `getServerSideProps` run?
questions.explanation: It runs server‑side on each incoming request, giving fresh data every time.

questions.question: What extra information does `getServerSideProps` receive compared to `getStaticProps`?
options: The request and response objects (req, res)
questions.explanation: It gets the `context` object containing `req`, `res`, `params`, `query`, etc., because it runs per request.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of SWR over `useEffect` + `fetch`?
options: It works only on the server
It automatically caches data, revalidates, and updates the UI
questions.explanation: SWR provides caching, background revalidation, error retry, and a simpler API.

questions.question: To enable Incremental Static Regeneration, you add the ______ key to the return object of `getStaticProps`.
questions.explanation: `revalidate: 60` tells Next.js to regenerate the page at most once every 60 seconds.

questions.question: How can you trigger ISR manually?
options: By calling an API route that uses `res.revalidate()`
questions.explanation: On‑demand ISR uses `res.revalidate('/path')` inside an API route, often secured by a secret.

questions.question: You can use `getStaticProps` and `getServerSideProps` on the same page.
questions.explanation: You can only use one data fetching method per page. They are mutually exclusive.

questions.question: Which scenario is NOT a good use case for client‑side data fetching?
options: A blog post that needs to rank in search engines
questions.explanation: Blog posts benefit from being pre‑rendered for SEO; client‑side fetching would hide content from crawlers.

questions.question: What does `notFound: true` return from `getStaticProps` do?
questions.explanation: It triggers the 404 page with a 404 status code.

questions.question: When using ISR, when does the regeneration happen?
options: On the next request after the cached page is older than the revalidate time
Only when the developer pushes new code
questions.explanation: ISR triggers regeneration when a request arrives and the page is older than the `revalidate` interval.

questions.question: What is the primary performance advantage of SSG over SSR?
options: Pages are served from a CDN, resulting in very low Time to First Byte
questions.explanation: Static pages can be cached on edge networks, giving instant responses without server processing.

questions.question: You should always use `getServerSideProps` because data freshness is more important than performance.
questions.explanation: Performance matters; use SSR only when you truly need request‑time data. Otherwise SSG or ISR is preferred.

questions.question: In the `getStaticPaths` return object, what does `paths` contain?
options: An array of all possible URLs
An array of objects with a `params` key matching the dynamic segment
questions.explanation: `paths: [{ params: { id: '1' } }, { params: { id: '2' } }]` defines which instances to pre‑render.

questions.question: The React Hook library recommended by the Next.js team for client‑side data fetching is ______.
questions.explanation: SWR (Stale‑While‑Revalidate) is created by the same team and integrates seamlessly.

questions.question: Which method would you use to fetch data on a page where the URL parameter `id` determines the content, and the page can be statically generated?
questions.explanation: Dynamic static pages need both: `getStaticPaths` to specify which `id` values to build, and `getStaticProps` to fetch data for each.

questions.question: What is 'hydration' in the context of Next.js?
options: The process where React attaches event listeners to pre‑rendered HTML
Re‑rendering the page on every click
questions.explanation: Hydration makes the static HTML interactive by linking it to the React component tree.

questions.question: You can use `getStaticProps` with `revalidate` on a page that uses `getServerSideProps`.
questions.explanation: These are different data fetching strategies and cannot coexist on the same page.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about `fallback: 'blocking'`?
options: The user sees a loading spinner
The page is generated on the server on the first request, then cached
All paths must be defined at build time
questions.explanation: 'blocking' means the server will wait until the page is generated before sending a response – no loading state on the client.
